# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

@startuml

title pa21 Model

class Alive {
    collectedExtraLives : List<Position>
    collectedGems : List<Position>
}
abstract class BoardElement {
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
abstract class Cell {
    position : Position
}
class Dead {
    minePosition : Position
}
abstract class Entity {
    owner : EntityCell
    setowner(owner : EntityCell) : EntityCell
}
class EntityCell {
    entity : Entity
    setentity(newEntity : Entity) : Entity
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
class ExtraLife {
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
class GameBoard {
    board : CellArray2D
    numCols : int
    numRows : int
    player : Player
    getCell1(row : int, col : int) : Cell
    getCell2(position : Position) : Cell
    getCol(col : int) : List<Cell>
    getEntityCell1(position : Position) : EntityCell
    getEntityCell2(row : int, col : int) : EntityCell
    getNumGems() : int
    getRow(row : int) : List<Cell>
}
class GameBoardController {
    gameBoard : GameBoard
    makeMove(direction : Direction) : MoveResult
    undoMove(prevMove : MoveResult) : void
}
class GameBoardView {
    gameBoard : GameBoard

    processUndo() : boolean

    getnumLives() : int

    increaseNumLives(delta : int) : int
    incrementNumDeaths() : int
    incrementNumMoves() : int
}

    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
class Invalid {
}
class Mine {
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}

}
class MoveStack {

    moves : List<MoveResult>

    peek() : MoveResult
    pop() : MoveResult
    push(move : MoveResult) : void
}
class Player {
    toASCIIChar() : char
    toUnicodeChar() : char
}
class Position {
    col : int
    row : int
    offsetBy1(dRow : int, dCol : int) : Position
    offsetBy2(offset : PositionOffset) : Position
    offsetByOrNull1(dRow : int, dCol : int, numRows : int, numCols : int) : Position
    offsetByOrNull2(offset : PositionOffset, numRows : int, numCols : int) : Position

class PositionOffset {
    dCol : int
    dRow : int
}

    toUnicodeChar() : char

enum Direction {
    UP

    LEFT
    RIGHT

A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::hasUnlimitedLives
Summary: Indicates whether the player has unlimited lives.
Algorithm:
  1. Return numLives < 0 (lives less than zero are treated as the unlimited-lives sentinel).
Related Features: GameState.numLives, GameState.UNLIMITED_LIVES
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if numLives < 0, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized.
Post-condition: No state change.

GameState::decreaseNumLives
Summary: Decreases the current number of lives by the given delta and returns the new life count. No effect when the player has unlimited lives.
Algorithm:
  1. If hasUnlimitedLives() is true, return Integer.MAX_VALUE without modifying numLives.
  2. Otherwise, numLives = numLives - delta.
  3. Return the new numLives.
Related Features: GameState.numLives, GameState.UNLIMITED_LIVES
Related Classes: GameState
Input: delta : int — the positive amount by which to decrease the life count; should be >= 0.
Output: int — the updated number of lives; Integer.MAX_VALUE if lives are unlimited.
Pre-condition: delta is non-negative; the game state is initialized.
Post-condition: numLives is reduced by delta unless the player has unlimited lives.

If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::hasUnlimitedLives
Summary: Indicates whether the player has unlimited lives.
Algorithm:
  1. Return numLives < 0 (lives less than zero are treated as the unlimited-lives sentinel).
Related Features: GameState.numLives, GameState.UNLIMITED_LIVES
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if numLives < 0, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized.
Post-condition: No state change.

GameState::decreaseNumLives
Summary: Decreases the current number of lives by the given delta and returns the new life count. No effect when the player has unlimited lives.
Algorithm:
  1. If hasUnlimitedLives() is true, return Integer.MAX_VALUE without modifying numLives.
  2. Otherwise, numLives = numLives - delta.
  3. Return the new numLives.
Related Features: GameState.numLives, GameState.UNLIMITED_LIVES
Related Classes: GameState
Input: delta : int — the positive amount by which to decrease the life count; should be >= 0.
Output: int — the updated number of lives; Integer.MAX_VALUE if lives are unlimited.
Pre-condition: delta is non-negative; the game state is initialized.
Post-condition: numLives is reduced by delta unless the player has unlimited lives.

GameState::incrementNumMoves
Summary: Increments the move counter by one and returns the new value.
Algorithm:
  1. numMoves = numMoves + 1.
  2. Return numMoves.
Related Features: GameState.numMoves
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None.
Output: int — the updated move count (>= 1 after the first increment).
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized.
Post-condition: numMoves is increased by one.

GameState::getNumGems
Summary: Returns the number of Gems still present on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Delegate to gameBoard.getNumGems() and return the result.
Related Features: GameState.gameBoard, GameBoard.board
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoard, Gem
Input: None.
Output: int — the count of remaining Gems on the board, always >= 0.
Pre-condition: The game board is initialized.
Post-condition: No state change; the count is returned.

GameState::hasWon
Summary: Indicates whether the player has won the game by collecting all Gems.
Algorithm:
  1. Return getNumGems() == 0.
Related Features: GameState.gameBoard, GameBoard.board
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoard, Gem
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true when no Gems remain on the board, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized.
Post-condition: No state change.

GameState::decrementNumLives
Summary: Convenience method that decreases the number of lives by exactly one and returns the new value; no effect when the player has unlimited lives.
Algorithm:
  1. Delegate to decreaseNumLives(1) and return its result.
Related Features: GameState.numLives
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None.
Output: int — the updated number of lives; Integer.MAX_VALUE if unlimited.
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized.
Post-condition: numLives is reduced by one unless the player has unlimited lives.

GameState::hasLost
Summary: Indicates whether the player has lost the game.
Algorithm:
  1. If hasUnlimitedLives() is true, return false.
  2. Otherwise, return numLives <= 0.
Related Features: GameState.numLives, GameState.UNLIMITED_LIVES
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if lives have reached zero or below in finite-lives mode, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized.
Post-condition: No state change.

GameState::increaseNumLives
Summary: Increases the current number of lives by the given delta and returns the new life count. In unlimited-lives mode, returns Integer.MAX_VALUE without modifying numLives.
Algorithm:
  1. If hasUnlimitedLives() is true, return Integer.MAX_VALUE.
  2. Otherwise, numLives = numLives + delta.
  3. Return the new numLives.
Related Features: GameState.numLives
Related Classes: GameState
Input: delta : int — the non-negative amount by which to increase the life count.
Output: int — the updated number of lives; Integer.MAX_VALUE if unlimited.
Pre-condition: delta is non-negative; GameState is initialized.
Post-condition: numLives is increased by delta unless the player has unlimited lives.

GameState::getnumLives
Summary: Returns the current number of lives, or Integer.MAX_VALUE if the player has unlimited lives.
Algorithm:
  1. If hasUnlimitedLives() is true, return Integer.MAX_VALUE.
  2. Otherwise, return numLives.
Related Features: GameState.numLives, GameState.UNLIMITED_LIVES
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None.
Output: int — the number of lives remaining, or Integer.MAX_VALUE for unlimited.
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized.
Post-condition: No state change; the life value is returned.

GameState::getGameBoardView
Summary: Returns the GameBoardView associated with this game state, used for rendering the board to the user.
Algorithm:
  1. Return the stored gameBoardView field.
Related Features: GameState.gameBoardView (implicit), GameBoardView.gameBoard
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardView, GameBoard
Input: None.
Output: GameBoardView — the view object that visualizes the current gameBoard.
Pre-condition: The GameState has been fully initialized, including the view.
Post-condition: No state change; a reference to the existing GameBoardView is returned.

GameState::getScore
Summary: Computes and returns the current score for the player using the game's scoring formula.
Algorithm:
  1. collectedGems = initialNumOfGems - getNumGems().
  2. initialBoardSize = numRows * numCols (of the current gameBoard).
  3. score = initialBoardSize + (collectedGems * 10) - (numMoves * 1) - (undoCount * 2) - (numDeaths * 4).
  4. Return the score (may be negative).
Related Features: GameState.initialNumOfGems, GameState.numMoves, GameState.numDeaths, GameState.gameBoard, MoveStack.popCount
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoard, MoveStack
Input: None.
Output: int — the computed score, which can be negative.
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized; initialNumOfGems and the board dimensions are set.
Post-condition: No state change; the score is returned based on the current counters and remaining gems.

GameState::incrementNumDeaths
Summary: Increments the death counter by one and returns the new value.
Algorithm:
  1. numDeaths = numDeaths + 1.
  2. Return numDeaths.
Related Features: GameState.numDeaths
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None.
Output: int — the updated death count (>= 1 after the first increment).
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized.
Post-condition: numDeaths is increased by one.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

Algorithm:
  1. If hasUnlimitedLives() is true, return Integer.MAX_VALUE without modifying numLives.
  2. Otherwise, numLives = numLives - delta.
  3. Return the new numLives.

Related Classes: GameState

# Operation Specifications
Position::offsetByOrNull2
Summary: Returns a new Position shifted by the given PositionOffset, or null if the resulting position would lie outside the board.
Algorithm:
  1. Call offsetByOrNull1(offset.dRow, offset.dCol, numRows, numCols) and return the result.
Related Features: Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: Position, PositionOffset
Input: offset : PositionOffset — a non-null PositionOffset; numRows : int — number of board rows; numCols : int — number of board columns.
Output: Position — the shifted Position if within bounds, or null otherwise.
Pre-condition: numRows and numCols represent the actual board dimensions.
Post-condition: No state change; a new Position or null is returned.

Position::offsetBy2
Summary: Returns a new Position shifted by the given PositionOffset, without bounds checking.
Algorithm:
  1. Call offsetBy1(offset.dRow, offset.dCol) and return the result.
Related Features: Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: Position, PositionOffset
Input: offset : PositionOffset — a non-null PositionOffset carrying dRow and dCol.
Output: Position — a new Position shifted by the offset.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: A new Position is returned; this Position is unchanged.

Position::offsetByOrNull1
Summary: Returns a new Position shifted by the given deltas, or null if the resulting position would lie outside the board of size numRows × numCols.
Algorithm:
  1. Compute newRow = this.row + dRow; newCol = this.col + dCol.
  2. If newRow < 0 or newRow >= numRows or newCol < 0 or newCol >= numCols, return null.
  3. Otherwise, return new Position(newRow, newCol).
Related Features: Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: Position
Input: dRow : int — delta in rows; dCol : int — delta in columns; numRows : int — number of rows in the board (>= 0); numCols : int — number of columns in the board (>= 0).
Output: Position — a new shifted Position if within bounds, or null if the shift would go out of bounds.
Pre-condition: numRows and numCols represent the actual board dimensions.
Post-condition: No state change; a new Position or null is returned.

Position::offsetBy1
Summary: Returns a new Position shifted by the given row and column deltas, without bounds checking.
Algorithm:
  1. Compute newRow = this.row + dRow.
  2. Compute newCol = this.col + dCol.
  3. Return new Position(newRow, newCol).
Related Features: Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: Position
Input: dRow : int — the delta in rows (can be negative, zero, or positive); dCol : int — the delta in columns.
Output: Position — a new Position whose row/col are this.row + dRow and this.col + dCol.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: A new Position is returned; this Position is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getRow
Summary: Returns a list of all Cells in the specified row of the board, ordered from left column to right column.
Algorithm:
  1. For each col from 0 to numCols - 1, fetch the Cell via getCell1(row, col).
  2. Collect these Cells into a List<Cell>.
  3. Return the list.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, GameBoard.numRows, GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, Wall, EntityCell, StopCell
Input: row : int — zero-based row index, 0 <= row < numRows.
Output: List<Cell> — list of length numCols containing all cells in the row from left to right.
Pre-condition: The row index is within the valid board boundaries.
Post-condition: No state change; a new list view of the row is returned.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary: Returns the Cell located at the given zero-based row and column indices on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the indices against numRows and numCols bounds.
  2. Look up the corresponding Cell from the internal CellArray2D.
  3. Return the Cell.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, GameBoard.numRows, GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, Wall, EntityCell, StopCell
Input: row : int — zero-based row index, 0 <= row < numRows; col : int — zero-based column index, 0 <= col < numCols.
Output: Cell — the Cell at the specified location (never null for valid coordinates).
Pre-condition: The row and col arguments are within the valid board boundaries.
Post-condition: No state change; a reference to the cell is returned.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary: Returns the count of Gem entities still present on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Iterate over all cells in board.
  2. For each EntityCell, check whether its entity is a Gem instance.
  3. Increment a counter for each Gem found.
  4. Return the counter.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, EntityCell.entity
Related Classes: Gem, EntityCell, Cell
Input: None.
Output: int — number of Gem entities remaining on the board; 0 if none; always >= 0.
Pre-condition: The board has been initialized.
Post-condition: No state change; the gem count is returned.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary: Returns the Cell at the given Position on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Extract the row and col from the Position.
  2. Delegate to getCell1(row, col) to fetch the Cell.
  3. Return the result.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: Cell, Position, Wall, EntityCell, StopCell
Input: position : Position — a non-null Position whose row/col are within the board bounds.
Output: Cell — the Cell at the given position.
Pre-condition: The position's coordinates are within the valid board boundaries.
Post-condition: No state change; a reference to the cell is returned.

GameBoard::getCol
Summary: Returns a list of all Cells in the specified column of the board, ordered from top row to bottom row.
Algorithm:
  1. For each row from 0 to numRows - 1, fetch the Cell via getCell1(row, col).
  2. Collect these Cells into a List<Cell>.
  3. Return the list.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, GameBoard.numRows, GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, Wall, EntityCell, StopCell
Input: col : int — zero-based column index, 0 <= col < numCols.
Output: List<Cell> — list of length numRows containing all cells in the column from top to bottom.
Pre-condition: The column index is within the valid board boundaries.
Post-condition: No state change; a new list view of the column is returned.

GameBoard::getEntityCell2
Summary: Returns the EntityCell located at the specified row and column on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Retrieve the Cell at (row, col) using getCell1.
  2. Cast/check that the Cell is an EntityCell.
  3. Return the EntityCell.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, GameBoard.numRows, GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: EntityCell, StopCell, Cell
Input: row : int — zero-based row index, 0 <= row < numRows; col : int — zero-based column index, 0 <= col < numCols.
Output: EntityCell — the EntityCell at the given coordinates.
Pre-condition: The cell at (row, col) is an EntityCell (not a Wall).
Post-condition: No state change; a reference to the EntityCell is returned.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary: Returns the EntityCell located at the given Position on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Obtain the Cell at the given Position using getCell2.
  2. Cast or check that the Cell is an EntityCell.
  3. Return the EntityCell.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: EntityCell, StopCell, Cell, Position
Input: position : Position — a non-null Position whose coordinates are within the board bounds and where an EntityCell is expected.
Output: EntityCell — the EntityCell at the specified position.
Pre-condition: The position refers to a board location that contains an EntityCell (not a Wall).
Post-condition: No state change; a reference to the EntityCell is returned.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getRow
Summary: Returns a list of all Cells in the specified row of the board, ordered from left column to right column.
Algorithm:
  1. For each col from 0 to numCols - 1, fetch the Cell via getCell1(row, col).
  2. Collect these Cells into a List<Cell>.
  3. Return the list.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, GameBoard.numRows, GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, Wall, EntityCell, StopCell
Input: row : int — zero-based row index, 0 <= row < numRows.
Output: List<Cell> — list of length numCols containing all cells in the row from left to right.
Pre-condition: The row index is within the valid board boundaries.
Post-condition: No state change; a new list view of the row is returned.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary: Returns the Cell located at the given zero-based row and column indices on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the indices against numRows and numCols bounds.
  2. Look up the corresponding Cell from the internal CellArray2D.
  3. Return the Cell.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, GameBoard.numRows, GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, Wall, EntityCell, StopCell
Input: row : int — zero-based row index, 0 <= row < numRows; col : int — zero-based column index, 0 <= col < numCols.
Output: Cell — the Cell at the specified location (never null for valid coordinates).
Pre-condition: The row and col arguments are within the valid board boundaries.
Post-condition: No state change; a reference to the cell is returned.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary: Returns the count of Gem entities still present on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Iterate over all EntityCells in board.
  2. For each EntityCell, check whether its entity is a Gem instance.
  3. Increment a counter for each Gem found.
  4. Return the counter.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, EntityCell.entity
Related Classes: Gem, EntityCell, Cell
Input: None.
Output: int — number of Gem entities remaining on the board; 0 if none; always >= 0.
Pre-condition: The board has been initialized.
Post-condition: No state change; the gem count is returned.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary: Returns the Cell at the given Position on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Extract the row and col from the Position.
  2. Delegate to getCell1(row, col) to fetch the Cell.
  3. Return the result.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: Cell, Position, Wall, EntityCell, StopCell
Input: position : Position — a non-null Position whose row/col are within the board bounds.
Output: Cell — the Cell at the given position.
Pre-condition: The position's coordinates are within the valid board boundaries.
Post-condition: No state change; a reference to the cell is returned.

GameBoard::getCol
Summary: Returns a list of all Cells in the specified column of the board, ordered from top row to bottom row.
Algorithm:
  1. For each row from 0 to numRows - 1, fetch the Cell via getCell1(row, col).
  2. Collect these Cells into a List<Cell>.
  3. Return the list.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, GameBoard.numRows, GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, Wall, EntityCell, StopCell
Input: col : int — zero-based column index, 0 <= col < numCols.
Output: List<Cell> — list of length numRows containing all cells in the column from top to bottom.
Pre-condition: The column index is within the valid board boundaries.
Post-condition: No state change; a new list view of the column is returned.

GameBoard::getEntityCell2
Summary: Returns the EntityCell located at the specified row and column on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Retrieve the Cell at (row, col) using getCell1.
  2. Cast/check that the Cell is an EntityCell.
  3. Return the EntityCell.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, GameBoard.numRows, GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: EntityCell, StopCell, Cell
Input: row : int — zero-based row index, 0 <= row < numRows; col : int — zero-based column index, 0 <= col < numCols.
Output: EntityCell — the EntityCell at the given coordinates.
Pre-condition: The cell at (row, col) is an EntityCell (not a Wall).
Post-condition: No state change; a reference to the EntityCell is returned.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary: Returns the EntityCell located at the given Position on the game board.
Algorithm:
  1. Obtain the Cell at the given Position using getCell2.
  2. Cast or check that the Cell is an EntityCell.
  3. Return the EntityCell.
Related Features: GameBoard.board, Position.row, Position.col
Related Classes: EntityCell, StopCell, Cell, Position
Input: position : Position — a non-null Position whose coordinates are within the board bounds and where an EntityCell is expected.
Output: EntityCell — the EntityCell at the specified position.
Pre-condition: The position refers to a board location that contains an EntityCell (not a Wall).
Post-condition: No state change; a reference to the EntityCell is returned.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
MoveStack::isEmpty
Summary: Indicates whether the MoveStack currently has no entries.
Algorithm:
  1. Return moves.isEmpty().
Related Features: MoveStack.moves
Related Classes: MoveStack, MoveResult
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if the stack contains no MoveResult entries, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The MoveStack is initialized.
Post-condition: No state change.

MoveStack::pop
Summary: Removes and returns the top MoveResult from the stack, also incrementing the popCount that tracks undo usage.
Algorithm:
  1. If moves is empty, return null.
  2. top = moves.remove(moves.size() - 1).
  3. popCount = popCount + 1.
  4. Return top.
Related Features: MoveStack.moves, MoveStack.popCount
Related Classes: MoveStack, MoveResult
Input: None.
Output: MoveResult — the removed top entry, or null if the stack was empty.
Pre-condition: The MoveStack is initialized.
Post-condition: The stack has one fewer entry; popCount has been incremented by one.

MoveStack::peek
Summary: Returns the top MoveResult of the stack without removing it.
Algorithm:
  1. If moves is empty, return null.
  2. Otherwise, return moves.get(moves.size() - 1).
Related Features: MoveStack.moves
Related Classes: MoveStack, MoveResult
Input: None.
Output: MoveResult — the top entry of the stack, or null if empty.
Pre-condition: The MoveStack is initialized.
Post-condition: No state change.

MoveStack::push
Summary: Pushes a MoveResult onto the top of the stack.
Algorithm:
  1. moves.add(move).
Related Features: MoveStack.moves
Related Classes: MoveStack, MoveResult
Input: move : MoveResult — the move to push; expected to be an Alive (undoable) move in normal use, may be non-null.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The MoveStack is initialized.
Post-condition: The given MoveResult is added to the top of the stack.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
StopCell::setentity
Summary: Overrides EntityCell.setentity to restrict which entities can be placed on a StopCell. A StopCell may only hold a Player entity; setting any other entity type is rejected.
Algorithm:
  1. If newEntity is non-null and is not an instance of Player, return the current entity without changing it (or otherwise refuse the assignment).
  2. Otherwise, delegate to the inherited EntityCell.setentity(newEntity) to perform the replacement and return the previous entity.
Related Features: StopCell (subclass of EntityCell), EntityCell.entity
Related Classes: StopCell, EntityCell, Player, Entity
Input: newEntity : Entity — the entity to place on the StopCell; only Player instances (or null) are accepted.
Output: Entity — the entity previously held by the cell.
Pre-condition: The cell is a StopCell on the board.
Post-condition: If newEntity is a Player (or null), the cell now contains it and its owner is updated; otherwise, the cell remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameController::processUndo
Summary: Reverts the most recent Alive move by delegating board restoration to the controller and updating state counters. Returns true if an undo was performed, false if no undoable move is available.
Algorithm:
  1. If moveStack.isEmpty() returns true, return false.
  2. Call moveStack.peek() to get the top MoveResult.
  3. If the result is not Alive (e.g., the top is invalid for undo), return false.
  4. Invoke gameBoardController.undoMove(top) to restore the board.
  5. For each Position in the Alive result's collectedExtraLives, call decreaseNumLives(1) to reverse life gains.
  6. Call moveStack.pop() to remove the entry from the stack.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: GameState.moveStack, GameState.numLives, GameState.popCount, GameState.gameBoard
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardController, MoveStack, Alive, MoveResult, Position, ExtraLife
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if an undo occurred, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized; if a move exists on top of the stack, it must be Alive.
Post-condition: The player position, collected Gems/ExtraLives, and finite ExtraLife gains are restored to the pre-move state; the top entry is removed from the MoveStack; popCount reflects the number of pops; numMoves is not decremented.

GameController::processMove
Summary: High-level handler for a player move. Delegates to GameBoardController.makeMove, then updates game-state counters and the MoveStack according to the move's outcome, and returns the resulting MoveResult.
Algorithm:
  1. Invoke gameBoardController.makeMove(direction) to obtain a MoveResult.
  2. If the result is Invalid, do not modify any counter and do not push to the MoveStack; return the Invalid result.
  3. If the result is Alive, call incrementNumMoves; for each collected ExtraLife in the Alive result, call increaseNumLives(1); push the Alive result onto the MoveStack; return the result.
  4. If the result is Dead, call incrementNumMoves and incrementNumDeaths; call decrementNumLives(); do not push to the MoveStack; return the result.
Related Features: GameState.numMoves, GameState.numDeaths, GameState.numLives, GameState.moveStack, GameState.gameBoard
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardController, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Direction, MoveStack, Position
Input: direction : Direction — the desired sliding direction.
Output: MoveResult — the outcome of the move (Alive, Dead, or Invalid).
Pre-condition: A GameState with a valid gameBoard, gameBoardController, and moveStack is available; the direction is non-null.
Post-condition: Counters and the MoveStack are updated to reflect the move (or unchanged for Invalid); the appropriate MoveResult is returned to the caller.

# Operation Specifications
GameController::processUndo
Summary: Reverts the most recent Alive move by delegating board restoration to the controller and updating state counters. Returns true if an undo was performed, false if no undoable move is available.
Algorithm:
  1. If moveStack.isEmpty() returns true, return false.
  2. Call moveStack.peek() to get the top MoveResult.
  3. If the result is not Alive (e.g., the top is invalid for undo), return false.
  4. Invoke gameBoardController.undoMove(top) to restore the board.
  5. For each Position in the Alive result's collectedExtraLives, call decreaseNumLives(1) to reverse life gains.
  6. Call moveStack.pop() to remove the entry from the stack.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: GameState.moveStack, GameState.numLives, GameState.popCount, GameState.gameBoard
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardController, MoveStack, Alive, MoveResult, Position, ExtraLife
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if an undo occurred, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: GameState is initialized; if a move exists on top of the stack, it must be Alive.
Post-condition: The player position, collected Gems/ExtraLives, and finite ExtraLife gains are restored to the pre-move state; the top entry is removed from the MoveStack; popCount reflects the number of pops; numMoves is not decremented.

GameController::processMove
Summary: High-level handler for a player move. Delegates to GameBoardController.makeMove, then updates game-state counters and the MoveStack according to the move's outcome, and returns the resulting MoveResult.
Algorithm:
  1. Invoke gameBoardController.makeMove(direction) to obtain a MoveResult.
  2. If the result is Invalid, do not modify any counter and do not push to the MoveStack; return the Invalid result.
  3. If the result is Alive, call incrementNumMoves; for each collected ExtraLife in the Alive result, call increaseNumLives(1); push the Alive result onto the MoveStack; return the result.
  4. If the result is Dead, call incrementNumMoves and incrementNumDeaths; call decrementNumLives(); do not push to the MoveStack; return the result.
Related Features: GameState.numMoves, GameState.numDeaths, GameState.numLives, GameState.moveStack, GameState.gameBoard
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardController, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Direction, MoveStack, Position
Input: direction : Direction — the desired sliding direction.
Output: MoveResult — the outcome of the move (Alive, Dead, or Invalid).
Pre-condition: A GameState with a valid gameBoard, gameBoardController, and moveStack is available; the direction is non-null.
Post-condition: Counters and the MoveStack are updated to reflect the move (or unchanged for Invalid); the appropriate MoveResult is returned to the caller.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Entity::setowner
Summary: Sets the owner (EntityCell) of this Entity and returns the previous owner. Used to maintain the bidirectional association between an Entity and the EntityCell that contains it.
Algorithm:
  1. Store the current owner reference.
  2. Assign the new owner parameter to the 'owner' field.
  3. Return the previously stored owner.
Related Features: Entity.owner
Related Classes: Entity, EntityCell
Input: owner : EntityCell — the new EntityCell that will own this Entity; must be non-null in normal use.
Output: EntityCell — the previous owner of this Entity (may be null if the entity was previously unowned).
Pre-condition: The caller has a valid EntityCell reference to assign.
Post-condition: The Entity's owner field is updated to the new EntityCell, and the previous owner is returned to the caller.

Related Classes: Entity, EntityCell

Pre-condition: The caller has a valid EntityCell reference to assign.
Post-condition: The Entity's owner field is updated to the new EntityCell, and the previous owner is returned to the caller.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoardController::undoMove
Summary: Reverts the board state for a single previously executed Alive move, restoring the player to its original position and re-placing the collected Gems and ExtraLives on their original cells.
Algorithm:
  1. If prevMove is not an Alive (or not undoable), do nothing.
  2. Move the Player entity from the newPosition back to the origPosition.
  3. For each Position in prevMove.collectedGems, re-place a Gem entity on that EntityCell.
  4. For each Position in prevMove.collectedExtraLives, re-place an ExtraLife entity on that EntityCell.
Related Features: GameBoard.player, GameBoard.board
Related Classes: GameBoard, Alive, Valid, MoveResult, Position, Player, Gem, ExtraLife, EntityCell
Input: prevMove : MoveResult — the result of the previously executed move to be undone; expected to be an Alive instance with non-null origPosition and collected lists.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The board state corresponds to the post-move state of prevMove; prevMove is undoable (Alive).
Post-condition: The board reflects the state immediately before prevMove was made: the player is at origPosition and the previously collected Gems/ExtraLives are back on their cells.

GameBoardController::makeMove
Summary: Executes an inertial sliding move on behalf of the player in the given Direction, collecting Gems/ExtraLives along the way, and returns a MoveResult describing the outcome.
Algorithm:
  1. Read the player's current position and the chosen Direction.
  2. Convert the direction to a PositionOffset (e.g., UP = (-1, 0), DOWN = (1, 0), LEFT = (0, -1), RIGHT = (0, 1)).
  3. Initialize empty lists for collectedGems and collectedExtraLives, and remember the original position.
  4. Compute the candidate next Position using Position.offsetByOrNull2 with board bounds. If null, the player is at the boundary and the move is Invalid — return Invalid.
  5. Check the cell at the next position. If it is a Wall, the move is Invalid (no movement occurred) — return Invalid.
  6. Otherwise, slide step-by-step: for each step, inspect the cell. If the cell is a Mine, stop sliding, return Dead with newPosition equal to the original position and minePosition set; discard any gem/extraLife collected in this step.
  7. If the cell is a StopCell, stop on that cell, and return Alive with newPosition on the stop cell, recording any gems/extraLives collected so far.
  8. If the cell contains a Gem, remove it from the board (setentity(null)) and record the Position in collectedGems.
  9. If the cell contains an ExtraLife, remove it from the board and record the Position in collectedExtraLives.
  10. If the cell is the board boundary (offsetByOrNull2 returns null) or a Wall, stop one cell before the wall/boundary and return Alive.
  11. Update the player position on the board (place the Player entity on the final cell and clear the starting cell).
  12. Return Alive with newPosition and the collected lists.
Related Features: GameBoard.player, GameBoard.board, GameBoard.getEntityCell2, GameBoard.getCell1
Related Classes: GameBoard, Player, Direction, Position, PositionOffset, Alive, Dead, Invalid, MoveResult, Gem, ExtraLife, Mine, Wall, StopCell, EntityCell, Valid
Input: direction : Direction — the sliding direction (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT).
Output: MoveResult — an Alive result on normal stopping, Dead on mine hit, or Invalid if the player could not move at all.
Pre-condition: A game board exists, a Player entity is placed on the board, and the direction is non-null.
Post-condition: For Alive moves, the player is repositioned to the final cell and collected Gems/ExtraLives are removed from the board. For Dead moves, the board is unchanged from before the move and the player stays at the original position. For Invalid moves, the board is completely unchanged.

  2. Convert the direction to a PositionOffset (e.g., UP = (-1, 0), DOWN = (1, 0), LEFT = (0, -1), RIGHT = (0, 1)).
  3. Initialize empty lists for collectedGems and collectedExtraLives, and remember the original position.
  4. Compute the candidate next Position using Position.offsetByOrNull2 with board bounds. If null, the player is at the boundary and the move is Invalid — return Invalid.
  5. Check the cell at the next position. If it is a Wall, the move is Invalid (no movement occurred) — return Invalid.
  6. Otherwise, slide step-by-step: for each step, inspect the cell. If the cell is a Mine, stop sliding, return Dead with newPosition equal to the original position and minePosition set; discard any gem/extraLife collected in this step.
  7. If the cell is a StopCell, stop on that cell, and return Alive with newPosition on the stop cell, recording any gems/extraLives collected so far.
  8. If the cell contains a Gem, remove it from the board (setentity(null)) and record the Position in collectedGems.
  9. If the cell contains an ExtraLife, remove it from the board and record the Position in collectedExtraLives.
  10. If the cell is the board boundary (offsetByOrNull2 returns null) or a Wall, stop one cell before the wall/boundary and return Alive.
  11. Update the player position on the board (place the Player entity on the final cell and clear the starting cell).
  12. Return Alive with newPosition and the collected lists.
Related Features: GameBoard.player, GameBoard.board, GameBoard.getEntityCell2, GameBoard.getCell1
Related Classes: GameBoard, Player, Direction, Position, PositionOffset, Alive, Dead, Invalid, MoveResult, Gem, ExtraLife, Mine, Wall, StopCell, EntityCell, Valid
Input: direction : Direction — the sliding direction (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT).
Output: MoveResult — an Alive result on normal stopping, Dead on mine hit, or Invalid if the player could not move at all.
Pre-condition: A game board exists, a Player entity is placed on the board, and the direction is non-null.
Post-condition: For Alive moves, the player is repositioned to the final cell and collected Gems/ExtraLives are removed from the board. For Dead moves, the board is unchanged from before the move and the player stays at the original position. For Invalid moves, the board is completely unchanged.
